bleed.label: Bleed week
bleed.why: Iron, folate or a warm, filling base — good for the pill-free week.

strength.label: Strength day
strength.why: 38 g+ protein — good after GAP or V-Burn.

light.label: Light dinner
light.why: Around 550 kcal or less — fits the light 20:00 dinner.

treat.label: Occasional
treat.why: Heavy — keep for a long-training day, not a regular slot.

recipes.title: Chorizo-Crusted Penne and Cheese
recipes.when: A big, rich lunch for a long-training day. Too heavy for dinner or every week.
swaps: Use sweet (dulce) chorizo — not picante — so it stays mild.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C and put a pan of salted water on to boil. Slice the shallot, grate the garlic and the cheddar.

Cook the penne for 12 minutes, then drain and toss with a little oil. While it cooks, fry the chorizo in a dry pan for 1–2 minutes until it releases its oil, then mix it with the panko, a drizzle of olive oil and black pepper.

In the same pan, soften the shallot for 3–4 minutes. Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually add the water and stock and simmer 1–2 minutes until thick. Off the heat, stir in the crème fraîche, oregano and cheddar until melted.
Stir the penne into the sauce (splash of water if thick), tip into a small ovenproof dish, scatter the chorizo crumb over and bake on the top shelf for 5–6 minutes until golden.

Meanwhile, wipe the pan and fry the green beans in a little oil for 2–3 minutes until charred. Add the garlic for 1 minute, a splash of water, cover and cook 4–5 minutes until tender. Serve alongside.

source.name: HelloFresh UK — Chorizo Crusted Penne n Cheese

recipes.title: Mediterranean Halloumi Pasta
recipes.when: Lunch. Spinach (iron) eaten with roasted tomatoes (vitamin C) helps you absorb the iron — a good bleed-week pick.
swaps: Added baby spinach to match your saved version (and for iron).
Tomatoes are roasted, not raw.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (or air fryer to 190°C). Toss the cherry tomatoes with the oil, oregano, salt and pepper on a small tray.
Roast the tomatoes until blistered — about 18 minutes in the oven, 12–15 in the air fryer.
Cook the penne in salted boiling water for 12 minutes. Keep a mug of pasta water before draining.
Dry-fry the halloumi in a non-stick pan for about 4 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides.
Drain the pasta and return to the pan. Stir in the cream cheese, lemon juice and a splash of pasta water, then the spinach until it wilts (about 1 minute).
Fold through the roasted tomatoes, halloumi and torn basil. Season with black pepper and serve.

source.name: Hungry Healthy Happy — Halloumi Pasta

recipes.title: Roasted Aubergine Hummus Bowls
recipes.when: Light dinner. Low in protein as written — add the eggs or extra chickpeas, especially on strength days.
swaps: Harissa → smoked paprika (no chilli).
Ras el hanout (cumin/coriander blend) → sweet smoked paprika + pinch of cinnamon.
Red onion is softened in lemon juice so it's milder.
Optional: add 2 eggs for +12 g protein.

steps.text: Cut the aubergine into large chunks and dry-fry in a large pan on high heat with a big pinch of salt, turning, until blackened on all sides (10–15 minutes).
Meanwhile, blend 60 g chickpeas with the roasted pepper, tahini, juice of ½ lemon, ½ tsp smoked paprika and a drizzle of olive oil until smooth. Season.
Finely shred the cabbage, thinly slice the onion and toss with the herbs, juice of the other ½ lemon, 1 tbsp olive oil and salt. (If adding eggs, boil them now for 7 minutes.)
Add the remaining chickpeas, the rest of the paprika, the cinnamon, a drizzle of oil and the honey to the aubergine. Toss for 3–4 minutes until collapsed and sticky. Toast the bread.
Spread the hummus in a bowl, pile on the aubergine and salad (and halved eggs), scatter with sesame seeds and serve with the toast.

source.name: Mob — Aubergine Hummus Bowl

recipes.title: Salmon & Asparagus Brown Rice Pilaf
recipes.when: Light dinner any week. Salmon gives omega-3 and B12 (useful while on the pill).
swaps: The source's flour-and-egg-yolk sauce is swapped for a lemon-mustard butter to keep it light and quick.
Uses a pouch of cooked brown rice to stay under 25 minutes (raw brown rice takes ~25 min on its own).

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (or air fryer to 190°C). Season the salmon and put it on a lined tray with a lemon slice on top.
Roast the salmon for 12 minutes (air fryer 8–10) until it flakes easily.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a pan and soften the finely chopped shallot for 3 minutes.
Add the rice and stock, stir and warm through for 3–4 minutes. Stir in the mustard and lemon zest.
Snap the woody ends off the asparagus and cook in a griddle pan or steam for 3–4 minutes until just tender.
Stir the snipped chives and a squeeze of lemon into the rice. Serve with the salmon and asparagus.

source.name: Tilda — Salmon & Asparagus Pilaf (adapted from 12 servings)

recipes.title: Mushroom & Pea Risotto
recipes.when: Warm and comforting for the bleed week. Low in protein — top with a fried egg or stir in white beans.
swaps: Optional: top with a fried egg (+6 g protein) or stir in 60 g cannellini beans (+5 g protein, +iron).

steps.text: Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Soften the chopped onion and garlic for 2 minutes, then add the mushrooms and cook until golden, about 3 minutes.
Stir in the rice and toast it for 1–2 minutes.
Add the hot stock a ladle at a time over medium-low heat, stirring often and adding more once it's absorbed. It takes about 18 minutes for the rice to become creamy but still slightly firm.
Add the peas for the last 4 minutes. If topping with an egg, fry it now.
Take off the heat, stir in the parmesan, season, rest 1 minute and scatter with herbs.

source.name: Birds Eye — Mushroom and Pea Risotto

recipes.title: Crispy Tofu Rice Bowls
recipes.when: Any week. Tofu gives iron and calcium; add a soft-boiled egg for more protein.
swaps: Chilli glaze and fresh chilli → honey-soy glaze, no heat.
Optional: a soft-boiled egg for +6 g protein.

steps.text: Rinse the rice, put it in a lidded pan with 150 ml water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on low for 10 minutes. Turn off and leave covered for 10 more.
Press the tofu between kitchen paper to remove water. Cut into 2 cm cubes and toss with the cornflour and a pinch of salt. Mix the soy, honey, vinegar and garlic in a cup.
Fry the tofu in the oil on medium-high for 8–10 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. (Boil the egg for 7 minutes alongside, if using.)
Pour in the honey-soy sauce and let it bubble for 1–2 minutes until sticky and coating the tofu.
Slice the cucumber and spring onion. Fill a bowl with rice, tofu and cucumber, then sprinkle with sesame and spring onion.

source.name: Barker's — Honey Soy Tofu Bowls

recipes.title: Mushroom Pasta Bake
recipes.when: Warm bleed-week lunch. It's 40 minutes, so make a double batch — the second portion is tomorrow's lunch.
swaps: Taleggio → mozzarella or any melting cheese you have.
Wine and truffle oil are optional.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan) and boil a pan of salted water.
Cook the pasta for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Keep 100 ml of the water, then drain.
Meanwhile, fry the onion in the oil until soft, then turn the heat up, add the mushrooms and cook until browned and any liquid has gone.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the thyme leaves and lemon zest. Add a splash of wine (if using) and let it bubble away.
Stir in the mascarpone, loosening with pasta water until it's like single cream. Wilt in the spinach, then add half the parmesan and the pasta.
Tip into an ovenproof dish, top with the mozzarella or taleggio and the rest of the parmesan, and bake for 12–15 minutes until bubbling and browned.

source.name: Hairy Bikers — Creamy Mushroom Pasta Bake

recipes.title: Chicken Souvlaki Rice
recipes.when: A top strength-day pick — 53 g protein, low fat. Works as lunch or a bigger dinner.
swaps: Diced raw tomato → cucumber + roasted red pepper.
Marinade cut to 10 minutes (or marinate overnight if you prep ahead).

steps.text: Put the rice on: rinse it, add 150 ml water and a pinch of salt, boil, cover and cook on low for 10 minutes, then rest covered for 10.
Mix the oil, lemon juice, vinegar, oregano, half the grated garlic and salt. Toss the chicken in it and leave for 10 minutes.
Make the tzatziki: grate a little cucumber, squeeze out the water and mix with the kefir, the rest of the garlic and the dill.
Cook the chicken in a hot griddle or frying pan for 7–8 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through (or air fry at 200°C for 10–12 minutes).
Dice the rest of the cucumber and slice the pepper. Plate the rice, chicken, veg and a big spoon of tzatziki.

source.name: Mel's Kitchen Cafe — Chicken Souvlaki Bowls

recipes.title: Pesto Pea Rigatoni
recipes.when: Lunch any week. Peas and spinach add folate and iron. On strength days add a chicken breast or 2 eggs.
swaps: Cherry tomatoes are roasted with the broccoli (cooked, so fine).

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan) and boil salted water. Halve any thick broccoli stems and grate the garlic.
Toss the broccoli and cherry tomatoes with oil, salt and pepper and roast for 10–12 minutes until crispy at the edges.
Cook the rigatoni for 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, fry the garlic in a little oil for 1 minute. Add the water and stock, simmer 1–2 minutes, then stir in the crème fraîche and bring back to the boil.
Drain the pasta into the sauce with the peas. Heat for 1–2 minutes, then wilt in the spinach and stir in the parmesan.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with pesto and top with the roasted broccoli and tomatoes.

source.name: HelloFresh UK — Presto Pesto Pea Rigatoni

recipes.title: Sticky Honey Chicken Rice Bowl
recipes.when: Strength-day lunch or dinner. 40 g protein with the scrambled egg.
swaps: No cilantro or green chilli — finished with spring onion and sesame instead.

steps.text: Put the rice on: rinse, add 150 ml water, boil, cover and cook on low for 10 minutes, then rest covered for 10.
Toss the chicken with 2 tsp soy, the oyster sauce, sugar, pepper and 2 tsp cornflour. Leave for at least 10 minutes. Whisk the glaze: 1 tbsp soy, stock, honey, minced garlic and 1 tsp cornflour.
Heat the oil on medium. Fry the white part of the spring onion for 1–2 minutes until fragrant, then remove it.
Add the chicken in a single layer and sear for 5–7 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through.
Stir the glaze, pour it in, turn the heat up and bubble for about 2 minutes until thick and sticky.
Meanwhile, softly scramble the egg in a small pan. Serve the chicken and egg on the rice with the spring onion greens and sesame.

source.name: Tiffy Cooks — Honey Garlic Glazed Chicken Rice Bowl

recipes.title: Garlic Butter Salmon
recipes.when: Lunch any week. Omega-3 and B12. Comes with green beans and carrot so you get your veg in.
swaps: Paprika is the sweet kind (no heat).

steps.text: Rinse the rice and add to a lidded pan with 150 ml cold salted water. Boil, then cover and cook on medium-low for 10 minutes. Take off the heat and leave covered for 10 more.
While it cooks, chop the parsley, cut the lemon into wedges, grate the garlic, trim the beans and cut the carrot into batons.
Fry the carrot and beans in a little oil for 2–3 minutes until charred. Add a splash of water, cover and cook 4–5 minutes until tender. Season and keep warm.
Wipe the pan, add half the butter and a little oil on medium-high. Fry the salmon for 4–5 minutes per side until cooked through. Season.

Add the rest of the butter, the garlic and paprika and cook for 1 minute. Squeeze in some lemon, add the parsley and veg and toss 1–2 minutes. Serve on the fluffed rice with the pan butter spooned over.

source.name: HelloFresh Ireland — Garlic Butter Salmon

recipes.title: Lemon Herb Halloumi Bowls
recipes.when: Bleed-week lunch: roasted sweet potato is the warm, grounding root veg the workshop suggests. Use the air fryer to save 10 minutes.
swaps: Peri peri → lemon, oregano and sweet smoked paprika (no chilli).
Fresh chilli removed.
Coriander → parsley.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (or air fryer to 200°C). Cut the sweet potato into bite-size chunks.
Toss with oil, juice of ½ lemon, half the oregano, the paprika and salt. Roast for 25–30 minutes (air fryer 18–20) until golden and soft.
Finely shred the cabbage and slice the spring onion. Toss with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of salt.

Mix the honey with the lemon zest, the rest of the oregano and the garlic powder. Fry the halloumi in a non-stick pan for 2–3 minutes per side until golden, brush with the honey mix and fry 1 more minute until sticky.
Warm the flatbread. Spread the hummus in a bowl and top with the sweet potato, slaw and halloumi. Finish with parsley, sesame and a lemon wedge.

source.name: Mob (via Aldi) — Peri Peri Halloumi & Sweet Potato Houmous Bowl

recipes.title: Halloumi Gyros
recipes.when: Quick light dinner any week.
swaps: Chilli flakes removed.
Raw tomato → roasted red pepper.
Herby chips skipped to keep it light (add them for a lunch version).

steps.text: Toss the halloumi slices with the honey, garlic powder, oregano and the lemon zest and juice.
Heat a griddle or non-stick pan on high and cook the halloumi for 2–3 minutes per side until charred.
Warm the flatbread on the hot pan for about 1 minute each side. Slice the cucumber, lettuce and pepper.
Spread the flatbread with tzatziki, add the lettuce, cucumber, pepper and halloumi, then wrap tightly in baking paper.

source.name: delicious. magazine — Halloumi Gyros with Herby Chips

recipes.title: Farfalle with Feta & Broad Beans
recipes.when: Bleed-week or pill-week lunch: broad beans give iron and folate, and lemon (vitamin C) helps absorb the iron.
swaps: Chilli flakes → black pepper and lemon zest.
Prosciutto added to match your saved version.

steps.text: Bring a pan of salted water to the boil. Blanch the broad beans for 3 minutes, lift them out with a slotted spoon and cool under cold water.
Cook the farfalle in the same water according to the packet (about 11 minutes). Keep a mug of pasta water.
Meanwhile, cook the sliced shallot in the oil for 5 minutes until soft and sweet. Slip the broad beans out of their skins (optional, but greener).
Add the drained pasta and beans to the shallots with a splash of pasta water, the lemon zest and juice, most of the feta and herbs. Stir over the heat until glossy.
Plate, tear over the prosciutto, then top with the rest of the feta, herbs and plenty of black pepper.

source.name: Waitrose — Summer Bean & Feta Pasta

recipes.title: Kale Green Sauce Rigatoni
recipes.when: Light dinner, great in pill weeks and the bleed week: kale gives folate, magnesium and iron with its own vitamin C. Add the white beans for protein.
swaps: Chilli removed.
White beans added for protein (or top with leftover chicken).

steps.text: Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Gently fry the smashed garlic in the oil in a small pan until golden (don't let it smoke), then tip both into a blender.
Blanch the kale in the boiling water for 3–4 minutes. Lift it into the blender with some water clinging to it and blend smooth with the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Cook the rigatoni in the same water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Add the beans for the last 2 minutes to warm. Keep a mug of pasta water.
Drain, return to the pan over low heat and stir through the kale sauce, loosening with pasta water. Taste — add lemon if it's bitter. Finish with parmesan, pepper and a drizzle of oil.

source.name: Vegkit — Freshly Picked Rigatoni with Kale Sauce

recipes.title: Falafel Rice Bowls
recipes.when: Fast light dinner. Chickpeas give iron, folate and magnesium — good in the bleed week.
swaps: Diced raw tomato → roasted red pepper.
Kefir tzatziki for extra protein.

steps.text: Heat the falafel as the pack says — oven, air fryer (about 8 minutes at 190°C) or pan.
Pour 75 ml boiling water over the couscous, cover for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork, olive oil, lemon and salt. (Or use cooked rice.)
Dice the cucumber and slice the pepper. Chop the parsley.
Build the bowl: couscous, falafel, cucumber and pepper, a big spoon of tzatziki, and parsley on top.

source.name: Jow — Fast Falafel & Tzatziki Bowl

recipes.title: Mediterranean Salmon Bowls
recipes.when: Strength-day dinner or lunch. A small handful of cherry tomatoes is fine.
swaps: Red onion left out (optional).
Marinade shortened to 10 minutes.

steps.text: Put the rice on (or use a pouch later). Mix 1 tbsp oil, 1 tsp honey, the soy, lemon zest, grated garlic and herbs. Coat the salmon and leave for 10 minutes.
Grill or roast the salmon at 200°C for 10–12 minutes (air fryer 8–10) until it flakes.
Whisk the dressing: lemon juice, 1 tbsp olive oil, ½ tsp honey, salt and pepper.
Halve the tomatoes, dice the cucumber and crumble the feta.
Fill a bowl with rice, salmon, tomatoes, cucumber, feta and olives, then drizzle with the dressing.

source.name: Tilda — Mediterranean Salmon Rice Bowl

recipes.title: Mild Chicken & Bean Rice Bowl
recipes.when: Top pick for strength days AND the bleed week: 55 g protein, plus black beans for iron, magnesium and folate. A squeeze of lime helps absorb the iron.
swaps: Frozen fajita mix → fresh chicken with a mild smoked-paprika rub (no chilli or cumin).
Coriander → parsley.
Raw tomato salsa → a warm smoky tomato sauce.

steps.text: Put the rice on: rinse, add 150 ml water and a pinch of salt, boil, cover and cook on low for 10 minutes, then rest covered for 10.
Rub the chicken with ½ tsp paprika, the garlic powder, oregano, salt and the oil.
Cook the chicken in a hot pan for 5–6 minutes per side until cooked through (or air fry at 200°C for 14 minutes). Rest, then slice.
In the same pan, warm the passata with the rest of the paprika and the honey for 1–2 minutes. Add the beans with a squeeze of lime and heat through.
Plate the rice, beans and sliced chicken, spoon the sauce over, and add parsley, lettuce and a lime wedge.

source.name: Tesco Real Food — Chicken Fajita Rice Bowl

recipes.title: Honey Lime Gyoza Wedges
recipes.when: An easy treat dinner. Low in protein — the eggs help. Not ideal after a strength day.
swaps: Sambal and sweet chilli sauce → honey-lime glaze (no heat).
Choose chicken gyoza and add 2 soft-boiled eggs for +12 g protein.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (or air fryer to 200°C). Cut the sweet potato into 2 cm wedges, skin on, toss with oil and salt, and roast for 25–30 minutes (air fryer 18–20), turning halfway.
Smash the cucumber with a rolling pin, cut into chunks and toss with the rice vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt.
Mix the honey, juice of ½ lime and 1 tsp soy for the glaze. Put the rest of the soy and a squeeze of lime in a little dish for dipping.
Toss the gyoza in a little oil and bake on the middle shelf for 15–18 minutes (air fryer 10–12), turning halfway. Boil the eggs for 7 minutes meanwhile.
Toss the hot gyoza in the honey-lime glaze. Toss the salad leaves with the cucumber. Serve everything together with the dipping sauce.

source.name: HelloFresh UK — Sweet Chilli Gyozas and Sweet Potato Wedges

recipes.title: Paprika Salmon & Sprout Slaw
recipes.when: Any week, and good in the bleed week: kale and sprouts give vitamin C and folate, with sweet potato as the warm root veg.
swaps: Bulgur → sweet potato fries to match your saved version.
Smoked paprika is the sweet kind (no heat).

steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (or air fryer to 200°C). Cut the sweet potato into fries, toss with oil, salt and ½ tsp paprika, and roast for 20–22 minutes (air fryer 15–18), shaking halfway.

Thinly slice the sprouts and shred the kale. Toss with lemon juice, half the grated garlic, the honey, the kefir or mayo, salt and pepper. Massage with your hands for 1 minute to soften the kale. Add apple matchsticks if using.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes until they pop.
Pat the salmon dry and season with the rest of the paprika, garlic, salt and pepper. Roast skin-side down for 10–12 minutes (or pan-fry 4 minutes skin-side + 3 minutes).
Plate the fries, slaw and salmon, and sprinkle over the seeds.

source.name: HelloFresh Canada — Paprika-Spiced Salmon & Apple Brussels Sprout Slaw

recipes.title: Garlic Butter Steak Rice
recipes.when: Best bleed-week pick: red meat gives haem iron, the type your body absorbs most easily. Have a side salad with lemon (vitamin C) to help.
swaps: Mentsuyu (Japanese soup base) → soy sauce + a pinch of sugar, so it's easy to find.
Garlic chips optional.

steps.text: If you don't have leftover rice, cook it now (rinse, 150 ml water, boil, cover 10 minutes, rest 10). Take the steak out of the fridge and season with salt and pepper.
Mix 1 tbsp soy, 1 grated garlic clove and a pinch of sugar for the steak sauce.
Melt 10 g butter in a pan on medium and cook the other 2 minced garlic cloves for 3 minutes, stirring, until fragrant but not brown.
Add the rice with 1 tsp soy and pepper, stir-fry to heat through, then press it flat and leave it to crisp underneath.
Meanwhile, sear the steak in a very hot pan with the oil for 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Rest it for 3 minutes with the last bit of butter on top.
Slice the steak, toss it in the sauce, pile it on the rice and finish with spring onion. Serve with a lemony side salad.

source.name: Just One Cookbook — Steak Garlic Rice

recipes.title: Sticky Hoisin Pork Steaks
recipes.when: Strength-day lunch or dinner. Pork adds zinc and B vitamins.
swaps: Sriracha mayo → lime mayo (no heat).
Green chilli removed — spring onion only.

steps.text: Put the rice on with 150 ml water and a pinch of salt: boil, cover and cook on medium for 10 minutes, then rest covered for 10.
Slice the spring onion, zest the lime, grate the garlic and trim the beans. Mix the hoisin, honey and 50 ml water. Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 2–3 minutes.
Stir-fry the beans in a little oil for 2–3 minutes until charred. Add the garlic for 1 minute, a splash of water, cover and cook 4–5 minutes. Squeeze over lime and keep warm.
Wipe the pan. Fry the seasoned pork for 2–3 minutes per side on medium-high, then 4–6 minutes on medium, turning. Pour in the glaze and bubble 2–3 minutes until sticky. No pink in the middle.
Mix the mayo with a squeeze of lime. Stir the lime zest through the rice. Slice the pork onto the rice with the beans, drizzle with lime mayo and top with sesame and spring onion.

source.name: HelloFresh UK — Sticky Hoisin Glazed Pork Steaks

recipes.title: Steak & Peppercorn Sauce
recipes.when: Bleed-week lunch (haem iron) or after a strength day. The air fryer brings it down to about 25 minutes.
swaps: Peppercorns are warm rather than chilli-hot. Use ½ tsp for a gentler sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (or air fryer to 200°C). Take the steak out of the fridge. Cut the potatoes into 2 cm chunks, skin on.
Toss the potatoes with oil and salt and roast for 25–30 minutes (air fryer 18–20), turning halfway.
With 10 minutes left, toss the green beans in oil and salt and roast on the middle shelf for 8–10 minutes.
Heat a frying pan on high. Season the steak and brown for 1 minute each side, then 1–2 minutes more each side for medium-rare. Rest under foil.

In the same pan on low, soften the chopped shallot for 2–3 minutes. Add the peppercorns for 1 minute, then the water and stock. Simmer until halved (2–3 minutes). Off the heat, stir in the crème fraîche.
Slice the steak and serve with the sauce poured over, the potatoes and the beans.

source.name: HelloFresh UK — Steak and Peppercorn Sauce

recipes.title: Steak Fajita Rice
recipes.when: Great in the bleed week: steak (haem iron) with peppers (vitamin C) is the best combination for absorbing iron.
swaps: Fajita/guacamole seasoning (chilli, cumin) → mild blend of sweet smoked paprika, garlic and oregano.
Cilantro → parsley.
Marinade cut from 1 hour to 10 minutes.

steps.text: Put the rice on: rinse, add 150 ml water, boil, cover and cook on low for 10 minutes, then rest covered for 10.
Mix the paprika, garlic powder, oregano, salt, juice of ½ lime and the oil. Coat the steak and leave it for 10 minutes. Slice the pepper and onion.
Cook the pepper and onion in a hot pan for 5–6 minutes until softened and charred at the edges. Set aside.
Turn the heat to high and sear the steak for 2–3 minutes per side for medium. Rest for 3 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.
Spoon the rice into a bowl, top with the peppers and steak, squeeze over the rest of the lime and scatter with parsley.

source.name: The Salty Cooker — Steak Fajita Rice Bowl

recipes.title: Curried Onion Hotdogs
recipes.when: A weekend treat. At 1,050 kcal for two, have one hotdog plus a big side salad for a normal lunch.
swaps: Curry powder cut to ½ tsp mild (or swap for sweet smoked paprika if you'd rather skip curry altogether).

steps.text: Melt the butter in a pan on medium and add the thinly sliced onion with a pinch of salt. Cook slowly, stirring now and then, for about 20 minutes until soft and sticky.
Meanwhile, cook the sausages in a pan, the oven or the air fryer (about 12–15 minutes at 190°C) until golden and cooked through.
Add the vinegar and sugar to the onions and cook 5 more minutes until jammy.
Mix the ketchup, mustard and curry powder.
Split the buns, spread with the onion jam, add the sausages, drizzle with the curried ketchup and sprinkle with chives.

source.name: Mob (via Aldi) — Curried Ketchup Hotdogs with Sticky Onion Jam

recipes.title: Air Fryer Sticky Pork Belly
recipes.when: Occasional lunch — pork belly is fatty. Have it with plenty of salad.
swaps: Made sticky rather than spicy: chilli oil and chilli flakes removed.
Renamed from 'Spicy' to match.
ingredients: Pork belly slices, rind off, 4 cm pieces

steps.text: Mix the soy, honey, hoisin, vinegar, sesame oil, ginger, garlic and five spice. Set 1 tbsp aside for glazing, then toss the pork in the rest. (Marinate up to 24 hours if you prep ahead.)
Put the rice on (rinse, 150 ml water, boil, cover 10 minutes, rest 10).

Preheat the air fryer to 180°C for 3 minutes. Lay the pork in a single layer and cook for 16–20 minutes, turning halfway, until the fat has rendered and the edges are caramelised. (Oven: 200°C for 25–30 minutes.)
Brush the hot pork with the reserved glaze straight away. Serve on the rice with salad and cucumber, scattered with spring onion and sesame.

source.name: Simple Home Edit — Air Fryer Sticky Pork Belly Bites

recipes.title: Cajun Rump Steak & Creamy Rigatoni
recipes.when: Big strength-day lunch (55 g protein) and a strong bleed-week pick: steak plus spinach for iron.
swaps: Cajun spice mix (cayenne) → mild home blend: sweet smoked paprika, garlic powder, thyme and oregano.

steps.text: Boil a kettle and take the steak out of the fridge. Grate the garlic and mix the spices.
Cook the rigatoni in salted boiling water for 12 minutes, then drain and toss with a little oil.
Meanwhile, fry the seasoned steak in a very hot pan for about 5 minutes for medium-rare, turning halfway. Rest under foil.

In the same pan on medium, cook the garlic, spice blend and tomato purée for 30 seconds. Add the crème fraîche, stock, sugar and water and simmer for 4–5 minutes. Wilt in the spinach, then stir in the parmesan and butter.
Stir in the pasta (splash of water if thick). Slice the steak and lay it on top.

source.name: HelloFresh UK — 21 Day Aged Rump Steak and Creamy Cajun Rigatoni

recipes.title: Spaghetti and Meatballs
recipes.when: Classic bleed-week lunch: beef (haem iron) in a cooked tomato sauce (vitamin C). Double it — the meatballs reheat well.
swaps: Beef only (the source mixes in sausage meat) and a shorter 12-minute simmer.
Tomatoes are cooked, so fine.

steps.text: Mix the mince with half the crushed garlic, half the parsley, the breadcrumbs, egg, salt and pepper. Roll into 8 small balls.
Brown the meatballs in the oil on all sides for about 5 minutes. Lift them out and pour off any excess fat.
Fry the rest of the garlic for a few seconds, add the tomatoes and a pinch of sugar and cook on moderately high heat for 5 minutes until jammy. Season.
Return the meatballs, cover and simmer on low for 12 minutes, adding a splash of water if it gets dry. Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti.
Stir most of the remaining parsley into the sauce. Serve over the spaghetti with parmesan and the last of the parsley.

source.name: BBC Good Food Middle East — Meatballs with Spaghetti

recipes.title: Miso Glazed Steak Bowl
recipes.when: Strength-day dinner and a bleed-week favourite: 45 g protein with haem iron, and lime for vitamin C.
swaps: Chilli flakes on top → sesame seeds.

steps.text: Cook the rice according to the packet and keep it warm.
Whisk the glaze: 1 tsp miso, 1 tsp honey, the soy, 1 tsp garlic paste and the sesame oil.
Stir the dressing: kefir, tahini, 1 tsp miso, 1 tsp honey, lime zest and juice, ½ tsp garlic and the spring onion. Toss the chopped cucumber in it.

Salt the steak and sear in a very hot pan until browned on both sides (about 2 minutes per side). Pour over the glaze and let it bubble, flipping every 30 seconds, until thick and coating (2–3 minutes). Rest for 3 minutes.
Plate the rice and cucumber salad, slice the steak on top, pour over the pan glaze and finish with sesame seeds.

source.name: Jules Sebastian — Miso Glazed Steak Bowls with Creamy Cucumber Salad
